proposed.text: A firewall is required to achieve a 3-hour fire-resistive occupancy separation between a warehouse and a condominium sharing a common wall. The wall is 20.00 m long. A building manager requests a 12.00 m² double door opening and a 4.00 m² service window. Are these openings compliant per PD 1096, Rule XII, Section 1204?

options.text: Yes — the total opening (16.00 m²) is less than 25% of the wall area
No — the 12.00 m² double door exceeds the maximum single opening of 10.00 m²
Yes — as long as 3-hour fire assemblies are installed at both openings
No — no openings are permitted in a 3-hour occupancy separation wall under any circumstances

proposed.rationale: Original question was already source-correct and substantive; the prior edit (source-audited-article-batch-048) was degenerate, with 1-character garbage in 3 of 4 option text fields and a nonsensical rationale. Restored the original verbatim. Original source rationale: The two limits operate independently: the 25%-of-length limit controls total opening width, while the 10.00 m² single-opening cap prevents any individual penetration from being so large that it defeats the wall's fire-separation function. A 4.00 m² service window alone would be compliant; the 12.00 m² door is the violation.
